client-value-trust.title: Client Value & Trust
client-value-trust.narrative: Clients have trusted CL for our human expertise — somatic depth, culture, strategy, growing in complexity. They now want integrated expertise with AI and technological change. Walking our walk as we learn becomes what we can offer them; clumsy AI use risks visible slop and broken trust.
sessions: How To Talk To Clients About AI
insights: Clients want CL to bring integrated human + AI expertise, not just legacy CL strengths.
Trust deficit when AI touches deliverables — even partial AI generation erodes confidence.
Case studies and sophisticated AI conversations named as concrete client-value paths.
conflicts: Move fast on AI experiments vs protect client trust.
Demonstrate AI fluency vs avoid visible workslop.
Client-first clarity vs CL's own uneven AI maturity.

quotes.text: If there's something which is generated by AI, even partially… there is a deficit of trust.
We need to have more sophisticated conversations on AI with clients… every case study is a brief for five other clients.
What is our obligation to support the conversation that stretches in between the stuff right in front of our face and the 10-year thing?

cl-expertise-human.title: Our CL Expertise (Human)
cl-expertise-human.narrative: Our value in the adult development world — somatic experience, depth each colleague brings, understanding of humans, organizations, culture, strategy, and growing in complexity. This remains vital to who we are and what clients have trusted.
sessions: If CL were AI Native.... what principles etc?
insights: Craft and relationships named as CL's distinguishing assets in a 'time for craft' framing.
Human sensing and connection as a whole field of information to explore with clients.
What makes CL special isn't bytecoding — it's relational and developmental depth.
conflicts: Protect the relational core vs augment with AI tools.
Scale support vs premium human relationship.
Repurpose existing frameworks vs invent new agentic-AI offerings.

quotes.text: That human connection, that human sensing that a participant can't do. And that's a whole lot, that's a whole field of new information to explore with the client.
I don't think it's CL's expertise to be bytecoding and to be coding stuff… what makes CL special isn't stuff that we've just spent the last few hours talking about.
Productivity without prosperity, execution without verification, capacity without constraint are the downsides of not attending to…

ai-expertise.title: Our Expertise with AI
ai-expertise.narrative: AI fluency varies widely across CL — some surf the edge, others feel overwhelmed and unsure how to talk about it. Building real expertise matters: ungrounded adoption can destroy sense-making and break client trust. Verification labor rises with output volume.
sessions: If CL were AI Native.... what principles etc?
Taking Stock of AI at CL - 2
insights: Verification labor may triple — expertise to catch AI errors becomes more valuable.
Many different perspectives and roles within CL create uneven fluency and overwhelm.
Building expertise through experimentation parallels the support we can offer clients.
conflicts: AI extends experts vs removes junior learning tasks.
Surfing the edge vs feeling left behind.
More AI drafts vs fewer people to read carefully.

quotes.text: The amount of labor required to verify what you're hearing and seeing is triple.
quotes.session: If CL were AI Native.... what principles etc?

quotes.text: I think one of the reasons why I was overwhelmed by all of this is that there are many different perspectives and role within CL.
I would also want it to help me build expertise.
quotes.session: If CL were AI Native.... what principles etc?

build-own-tools.title: Build our own tools
build-own-tools.narrative: At the intersection of human and AI expertise, CL can build tools only we can build — for ourselves and for clients. Camp surfaced 10–20 internal tools already; some become client offerings that deepen our value.
insights: CL-values coaching tool alongside live coaches imagined explicitly in client implications.
Productized workshop experiments (e.g. Kinevan) to test with ourselves and clients.
Tools at the intersection of CL practice and AI lens on familiar frameworks.
conflicts: Build bespoke vs buy off-the-shelf.
Fall in love with tools vs focus on client need.
Scale internal experiments vs maintain craft quality.

quotes.text: What if there was something designed with CL values, principles, that was another coaching tool to use alongside our live coaches?
Building a little product that is the Kinevan AI workshop… test that with ourselves and with some clients.
I wasn't really sure why we needed it and if we need to build our own. I think sometimes we fall in love with tools rather than just buy the thing.

culture-language.title: Building our own culture & language of AI expertise
culture-language.narrative: The AI Pedal aims to help CL build shared culture and language — competency through experimentation, learning together across differences without othering or judging, generating trust and intimacy in the challenge of AI transformation.
sessions: How To Talk To Clients About AI
insights: Messy-but-real learning: poetry, humor, tech glitches, candid fear in live conversation.
Getting usefulness somewhere accessible probably outweighs overwhelm — but structure is nascent.
How we talk about AI reflects our journey of transformation individually and as an organization.
conflicts: Move fast where some feel clarity vs not leave others behind.
Upbeat energy vs grief/endings language.
Global comparison vs local specificity.

quotes.text: For those of you that find this overwhelming, like me, read whatever calls to you… don't feel like you need to read and digest it all.
Getting usefulness somewhere is, somewhere accessible by many probably outweighs the overwhelm.
In terms of what I hope we walk away with is some themes or experiments that people could literally sign up for.

risks-fears.title: Risks & Fears
risks-fears.narrative: Clients worry about slop; CL worries about ungrounded adoption breaking sense-making and trust. Fears around AI transformation need space — not moving too fast and leaving people behind, nor letting confusion slow clarity where we're ready to move.
sessions: How To Talk To Clients About AI
What can we do for our clients? Afternoon response to morning session
insights: Explicit room to speak fears in client-facing and internal conversations.
Workslop and discernment cynicism when language outruns practice.
Grief for disappearing roles — death doulas for the messy middle.
conflicts: Name fears vs keep conversations forward-looking.
Caution vs acceleration inside CL.
Transparency vs vulnerability with clients.

quotes.text: I think holding space for that — even letting people speak up their fears.
quotes.session: How To Talk To Clients About AI

quotes.text: If I'm a user of AI and not a producer of AI, and I'm also not completely sold on the hype…
quotes.session: How To Talk To Clients About AI

quotes.text: We need death doulas for the roles that are disappearing… walk them through the messy middle and midwife what comes next.

safety-governance.title: Safety & Governance
safety-governance.narrative: As we develop AI expertise and tech infrastructure, safety and governance help us build strongly without stepping into the risks we fear — data sovereignty, approved tools, ethical integration aligned with CL values.
sessions: Rules and Guidelines for use of AI Apps
what can we do for our clients? afternoon response to morning
insights: CL AI app rules name recording/LLM data-leak risk and approved-tool requirements.
Data sovereignty matters especially for Indigenous traditional knowledge and regional contexts.
Non-exec director programs on governing AI — what they need to know, not just policy writing.
conflicts: Push forward vs safety/ethics conversation (varies by region).
US-hosted convenience vs regional sovereignty.
Governance frameworks vs practitioner experimentation speed.

quotes.text: Data sovereignty requirements are checked and any issues are addressed… AI Learning can be turned OFF… Data is deletable.

quotes.text: Sovereignty particularly matters for Indigenous people… traditional knowledge… being put into data centers.
We came up with, like four programs for non-exec directors… governing AI. Not the know-how to write risk policies, but kind of what they need to know.

tech-infrastructure.title: Tech infrastructure
tech-infrastructure.narrative: Building bespoke technology like CLara supports our learning journey and augments the feedback loop in ways we couldn't when we couldn't build our own tech. Consolidation amid tool sprawl is both opportunity and risk.
sessions: Rules and Guidelines for use of AI Apps
insights: CLara enables simultaneous shared access to transcripts and harvest data.
Tool sprawl ('cambrian explosion') vs possible consolidation point.
Regional relays use CLara as upload/harvest infrastructure.
conflicts: Consolidate on CLara vs distributed tool ecosystem.
Platform depth vs client go-to-market speed.
Capture for harvest vs minimize sensitive data exposure.

quotes.text: To have a tool we could all use simultaneously together on the same data… normally I would put all the transcripts into a cloud project, but you can't access it at the same time as I am.
America submitted everything on to Clara, and once we are done, we're going to upload everything on to Clara.
The possibility set is that we have so many distributed tools… is there a possible point of consolidation… Even all our world calls.

support-business-ops.title: Support business operations
support-business-ops.narrative: Tools we build for ourselves can support go-to-market, competitor analysis, operational efficiencies, and running the organization — which in turn helps us identify clients and meet their needs efficiently and safely.
sessions: discussion on AI and client needs
insights: Go-to-market excitement alongside regional hesitation in relay conversations.
Listing places where we can trust AI to help become more efficient with existing work.
Operational efficiency supports client identification and organizational viability.
conflicts: Go-to-market speed vs demonstrate internally first.
Operational AI vs protect sensitive client data.
Efficiency gains vs verification labor.

quotes.text: Oh, I'm really interested in the go-to-market, because this feels like such a big opportunity for us.
Can we list some places where we can trust AI to actually help us become more efficient with the work that we already do?
